questions.stem: In the linear function y = a + bx, the parameter b is:
options: the starting value of x in the model
the slope, the change in y per unit increase in x
the y-intercept, the value of y when x = 0
the x-intercept, the value of x when y = 0
questions.explanation: In y = a + bx, a is the initial value, the y-intercept, and b is the constant rate of change, the slope. Each increase of 1 in x changes y by b.

questions.stem: An electrician charges C = 40 + 25h dollars for a job lasting h hours. The 40 represents:
options: a charge of $40 for each hour
questions.explanation: The 40 is the value of C when h = 0, so it is charged even before any time is worked: a fixed fee. The hourly rate is the slope, $25.

questions.stem: The slope of the line through (1, 3) and (4, 12) is:
questions.explanation: Slope = rise ÷ run = (12 − 3) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Putting the run over the rise gives 1/3, and 9 is the rise alone.

questions.stem: The y-intercept of the line 2x + 5y = 20 is:
questions.explanation: On the y-axis x = 0, so 5y = 20 and y = 4. The value 10 is the x-intercept, and −2/5 is the slope.

questions.stem: The graph of a linear function with a negative slope:
questions.explanation: A negative slope means y decreases as x increases, so the line falls from left to right. A horizontal line has a slope of zero.

questions.stem: A step graph is the best model for:
options: the distance travelled at a constant speed
an asset’s value under flat rate depreciation
the height of a candle burning steadily
parking fees charged per hour or part of an hour
questions.explanation: A charge for each hour or part hour stays fixed across an interval, then jumps, which is a step graph. A constant speed, steady burning and flat rate depreciation all change at a constant rate, which is a straight line.

questions.stem: On a graph, the solution of a pair of simultaneous linear equations is:
options: the point where the two lines intersect
the y-intercept of each of the lines
the slope of each of the lines
the x-intercept of each of the lines
questions.explanation: The intersection point lies on both lines, so its coordinates satisfy both equations at once. The intercepts each satisfy only one equation.

questions.stem: Two lines have the same slope and different y-intercepts. As simultaneous equations they have:
options: one solution, where the lines cross
infinitely many solutions on one line
two solutions, one for each intercept
no solution, because the lines are parallel
questions.explanation: Equal slopes and different intercepts give parallel lines that never meet, so no point satisfies both equations. Infinitely many solutions occur only when the two lines are the same line.

questions.stem: Which equation is a linear relation?
questions.explanation: A linear relation has x only to the power 1, so its graph is a straight line. The others are a parabola, a hyperbola and an exponential curve.

questions.stem: A piecewise linear graph is the best model when a quantity:
options: stays at the same value for the whole domain
doubles in value at regular time intervals
changes at constant rates that differ between intervals
changes at the same constant rate throughout
questions.explanation: Each line segment has its own constant slope, so a piecewise linear graph suits rates that are steady within an interval but change between intervals, such as tax scales. One constant rate throughout is a single straight line.

questions.stem: The x-intercept of y = 6 − 2x is:
questions.explanation: On the x-axis y = 0, so 0 = 6 − 2x and x = 3. The value 6 is the y-intercept, and −2 is the slope.

questions.stem: The line with y-intercept 5 and slope −2 has equation:
questions.explanation: In y = a + bx, a is the y-intercept and b the slope, so a = 5 and b = −2. Swapping the two gives y = −2 + 5x, a line with slope 5.

questions.stem: On a distance–time graph, a horizontal line segment shows that the object is:
questions.explanation: A horizontal segment means the distance is not changing as time passes, so the object has stopped. A constant speed shows as a sloping straight segment.

questions.stem: The line through (2, 7) and (6, 19) has equation:
questions.explanation: The slope is (19 − 7) ÷ (6 − 2) = 3. Then 7 = a + 3 × 2 gives a = 1. Using the point’s y-value, 7, as the intercept forgets that x = 2 there, not 0.

questions.stem: A gym charges a $60 joining fee and $15 per week. The total cost C, in dollars, for w weeks is:
questions.explanation: The $60 is paid once, so it is the initial value, and $15 is added each week, so it is the slope. C = 15 + 60w would charge $60 every week.

questions.stem: A gym’s total cost is C = 60 + 15w dollars for w weeks. After how many weeks has a member paid $375 in total?
questions.explanation: Solve 60 + 15w = 375: 15w = 315, so w = 21. Dividing 375 by 15 to get 25 ignores the joining fee.

questions.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations x + y = 10 and x − y = 4.
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives 2x = 14, so x = 7, and then y = 10 − 7 = 3. The pair x = 3, y = 7 fails the second equation, since 3 − 7 = −4.

questions.stem: A school sells 40 tickets to a play: adults pay $12 and children pay $7. Takings are $405. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: With a adult tickets, 12a + 7(40 − a) = 405, so 5a + 280 = 405 and a = 25. The 15 is the number of child tickets.

questions.stem: The equation 3x + 2y = 12, written in the form y = a + bx, is:
questions.explanation: Subtract 3x to get 2y = 12 − 3x, then divide every term by 2: y = 6 − 1.5x. Forgetting to divide the 12 as well as the 3x gives the wrong intercept.

questions.stem: The depth of snow, d cm, t hours after it starts melting is d = 85 − 2.5t. The 2.5 tells us that:
options: the snow is 2.5 cm deep at the start
the snow takes 2.5 hours to melt
the depth falls by 2.5 cm each hour
the depth rises by 2.5 cm each hour
questions.explanation: The slope is −2.5, so each hour the depth changes by −2.5 cm: it falls by 2.5 cm. The starting depth is the intercept, 85 cm.

questions.stem: A simplified tax scale charges nothing on the first $20 000 of income and 20 cents per dollar on income from $20 000 to $50 000. The tax on an income of $35 000 is:
questions.explanation: Only the $15 000 above $20 000 is taxed: 0.2 × 15 000 = $3000. Taxing the whole $35 000 at 20 cents per dollar gives $7000.

questions.stem: Parking costs $4 for the first hour or part of an hour, then $3 for each extra hour or part of an hour. The cost of parking for 3 hours 20 minutes is:
questions.explanation: After the first hour, the remaining 2 hours 20 minutes starts three more hours, so the cost is 4 + 3 × 3 = $13. Charging only the two full extra hours gives $10, but part hours count.

questions.stem: A taxi charges a $4.20 flag fall plus $2.10 per kilometre. The fare for a 12 km trip is:
questions.explanation: Fare = 4.20 + 2.10 × 12 = 4.20 + 25.20 = $29.40. The value $25.20 leaves out the flag fall.

questions.stem: A table of values has x = 0, 1, 2, 3 and y = 4, 7, 10, 13. The rule is:
questions.explanation: When x = 0, y = 4, so the intercept is 4, and y rises by 3 for each step in x, so the slope is 3. The rule 3 + 4x swaps the two.

questions.stem: A small business has costs C = 500 + 4n and revenue R = 9n dollars for n items sold. The break-even number of items is:
questions.explanation: Break-even is where revenue equals cost: 9n = 500 + 4n, so 5n = 500 and n = 100. Dividing 500 by the cost per item, 4, gives 125, which ignores the revenue.

questions.stem: The lines y = 2x + 3 and 4x − 2y = 6 have how many points of intersection?
questions.explanation: Rearranging 4x − 2y = 6 gives y = 2x − 3. Both lines have slope 2 but different intercepts, so they are parallel and never meet.

questions.stem: The solution of 2x + 3y = 13 and x − y = −1 is:
questions.explanation: From the second equation x = y − 1. Substituting: 2(y − 1) + 3y = 13, so 5y = 15, y = 3 and x = 2. The points (5, 1) and (−1, 5) satisfy the first equation only.

questions.stem: A 30 cm candle burns down at 2.5 cm per hour, so its height is h = 30 − 2.5t after t hours. A suitable domain for the model is:
questions.explanation: The model stops making sense when the candle is gone: 30 − 2.5t = 0 at t = 12. Beyond that the rule gives negative heights, so t ≥ 0 alone is too wide.

questions.stem: The line 4x − 3y = 24 crosses the axes at:
questions.explanation: Setting y = 0 gives 4x = 24, so x = 6. Setting x = 0 gives −3y = 24, so y = −8. Losing the negative sign gives (0, 8).

questions.stem: Bike hire costs $12 per hour, with part hours charged pro rata, up to a maximum of $50 per day. The graph of cost against hours hired in one day is:
options: horizontal at $50 from the start of the hire
a line rising to $50 at about 4.2 hours, then horizontal
a line rising to $50 at 4 hours, then falling
steps rising by $12 every hour with no limit
questions.explanation: The cost rises at $12 per hour until 12t = 50, at t ≈ 4.2 hours, then the cap holds it at $50, a horizontal segment. This two-piece graph is piecewise linear.

questions.stem: Suppose one Australian dollar buys 0.65 US dollars. How many Australian dollars are needed to buy 130 US dollars?
questions.explanation: Australian dollars = 130 ÷ 0.65 = 200. Multiplying instead, 130 × 0.65 = 84.50, converts in the wrong direction.

questions.stem: A simplified tax scale: no tax on the first $20 000; 20 cents per dollar from $20 000 to $50 000; $6000 plus 30 cents per dollar over $50 000. The tax on $65 000 is:
questions.explanation: The $6000 covers the tax on income up to $50 000, then the extra $15 000 is taxed at 30 cents: 6000 + 0.3 × 15 000 = $10 500. Taxing all $65 000 at 30 cents gives $19 500.

questions.stem: A business has costs C = 500 + 4n and revenue R = 9n dollars for n items sold. How many items must be sold to make a profit of $1000?
questions.explanation: Profit = R − C = 9n − (500 + 4n) = 5n − 500. Setting 5n − 500 = 1000 gives n = 300. The answer 200 ignores the fixed cost of $500.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides 12 km in 30 minutes, rests for 15 minutes, then rides 18 km in 45 minutes. The average speed for the whole trip is:
questions.explanation: The total distance is 30 km and the total time is 90 minutes, or 1.5 hours, so the average speed is 30 ÷ 1.5 = 20 km/h. Leaving out the rest gives 24 km/h, the speed while moving.

questions.stem: Plan A costs $20 plus $0.50 per GB of data. Plan B costs $35 plus $0.20 per GB. Which statement is correct?
options: They cost the same at 75 GB; above that Plan A is cheaper.
They cost the same at 50 GB; above that Plan B is cheaper.
They cost the same at 50 GB; above that Plan A is cheaper.
They cost the same at 30 GB; above that Plan B is cheaper.
questions.explanation: Solve 20 + 0.5g = 35 + 0.2g: 0.3g = 15, so g = 50. Plan B has the smaller rate per GB, so beyond 50 GB it costs less.

questions.stem: The line through (−2, 5) and (4, −7) has equation:
questions.explanation: The slope is (−7 − 5) ÷ (4 − (−2)) = −12 ÷ 6 = −2. Then 5 = a − 2 × (−2) = a + 4, so a = 1. Getting 9 comes from a sign error with the −2.

questions.stem: Electricity costs a daily supply charge of $1.10, plus 28 cents per kWh for the first 10 kWh each day and 35 cents per kWh after that. The cost for a day using 16 kWh is:
questions.explanation: Cost = 1.10 + 10 × 0.28 + 6 × 0.35 = 1.10 + 2.80 + 2.10 = $6.00. Charging all 16 kWh at 28 cents gives $5.58, which ignores the higher second rate.

questions.stem: Three pens and two notebooks cost $13. Two pens and five notebooks cost $21.50. The cost of one notebook is:
questions.explanation: With pens p and notebooks n: 3p + 2n = 13 and 2p + 5n = 21.5. Multiplying to 6p + 4n = 26 and 6p + 15n = 64.5, then subtracting, gives 11n = 38.5, so n = 3.50. A pen is $2.00.

questions.stem: Postage is $3 up to 250 g, $5 over 250 g up to 500 g, and $8 over 500 g up to 1 kg. Compared with posting two 300 g parcels, one 600 g parcel costs:
questions.explanation: Two 300 g parcels are each in the $5 step, $10 in all. One 600 g parcel is in the $8 step, so it costs $2 less. On a step graph the cost depends only on which interval the mass falls in.

questions.stem: A plumber charges $150 for a 2-hour job and $270 for a 5-hour job, using a call-out fee plus an hourly rate. The call-out fee and hourly rate are:
questions.explanation: The hourly rate is the slope: (270 − 150) ÷ (5 − 2) = $40. Then 150 = a + 40 × 2 gives a call-out fee of $70. A rate of $60 with $30 fits the 2-hour job but not the 5-hour one.
